name: Multi-factor authentication
description: A password alone is not enough to log in. Users also confirm on their phone.

name: Security awareness training
description: Teach employees to spot fake emails and report them.

name: Email filtering
description: Scan incoming email and quarantine known malicious links and attachments.

name: Patch management
description: Keep every server and PC updated so known vulnerabilities are fixed.

name: Web application firewall
description: Filter web traffic and block requests that look like attacks, such as SQL injection.

name: Login rate limiting
description: Lock out anyone who fails to log in too many times in a row.

name: Network firewall
description: Close every port that does not need to be open to the internet.

name: Least privilege
description: Give every employee only the access their job needs, and remove admin rights from everyone else.

name: Network segmentation
description: Split the network into zones, so a hacked office PC cannot reach the database.

name: Endpoint detection and response
description: Security software on every machine that watches for suspicious behaviour and can stop it.

name: Central logging and alerts
description: Collect logs from every server in one place and raise an alert when something looks wrong.

name: Offline backups
description: Keep daily copies of the data offline, so the company can restore it instead of paying a ransom.

name: Block Office macros
description: Office refuses to run macros in files that came from the internet.

name: USB device control
description: Computers only accept USB sticks the company has approved.

name: Data loss prevention
description: Watches for sensitive files leaving the company, by email, upload or USB, and stops them.

name: Banned password list
description: Nobody can pick passwords like 'Summer2026!' or the bank's name.

name: Phishing-resistant MFA
description: Hardware security keys. A stolen password or a tapped approval is useless without the physical key.

name: Strong service account passwords
description: Service accounts get long random passwords that cannot be cracked offline.

name: LAPS and Credential Guard
description: Every machine gets a different local admin password, and Windows hides password hashes from memory.

name: Tiered admin model
description: Domain admins only log in to domain controllers, so their passwords never sit on ordinary PCs.

name: Honeytokens
description: Fake accounts and passwords that nobody should ever touch. Any use of them sets off an alarm.

name: Conditional access
description: Cloud logins are only allowed from bank laptops and expected countries.

name: Vendor access control
description: The IT vendor only gets access when the bank switches it on, and every session is recorded.

name: Payment call-back checks
description: Any new or changed bank account is confirmed by phone, using a number already on file.

name: 24/7 security operations center
description: A team watches the alerts day and night and reacts within minutes.
